quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. It means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What can you do from the center lane?

options.text: You may make left turns.
You may make U-turns.
You may pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may make left turns.
questions.explanation: This lane is only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it to pass other cars or drive straight.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to a driver?

options.text: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and makes it harder to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and makes your judgment worse.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, or near intersections. Never pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights. Never pass in any no passing zone.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Pull to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: What should drivers do when preparing to turn left?

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. Move to the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When must you use your turn signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when leaving a parking space, entering a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: You are on a divided multilane highway and see an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move to create space for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to create space for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, slow down and create a clear path. Stop and let it pass. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: How should you merge into heavy freeway traffic?

options.text: Use side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to freeway speed and yield to traffic already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging to make sure you have room to merge safely.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Look for a way around lowered gates.
Assume no trains are near and continue normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell you a train might be coming. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: You must stop for a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if the pedestrian is on your side of the road.
Only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
If the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
Only if a "Walk" signal is showing.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop for pedestrians crossing at any marked or unmarked crosswalk. Let them cross safely before you continue.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal a lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To change lanes safely, signal first, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard immediately.
Steer straight and slowly lift your foot off the gas pedal.
Maintain your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slowly lift your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake hard until you have control. Then brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely:

options.text: A deaf person.
Conducting a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind person.
questions.explanation: Always yield to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog. Give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Pass faster than smaller vehicles going downhill.
Turn with a smaller radius than smaller vehicles.
Pass faster than smaller vehicles going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what ensures safe driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home from a friend who hasn't been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who hasn't been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid driving while impaired is to arrange a ride with a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your system. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: To avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.
Flash your lights at them.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on the sides and back. Stay out of these areas by not driving alongside them and not tailgating.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Go through if no traffic is crossing.
Continue driving. You have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights warn of dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: On a freeway, if you miss your turn or exit, you should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Continue to the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on a freeway. Continue until you reach the next exit or a safe location to turn around.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving ability compared to other factors?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol affect your driving ability in similar ways. Being awake for 18 hours affects driving like having a blood alcohol level of 0.05%. Being awake for 24 hours affects driving like having a blood alcohol level of 0.10%.

questions.question: What should you do when a police officer stops you?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped by police. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor traffic safety problem.
A serious traffic safety problem.
Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: A serious traffic safety problem.
questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely when you drink alcohol or use drugs. Impaired driving endangers both yourself and others on the road.

questions.question: What does the posted speed limit show?

options.text: Only a recommended driving speed.
The exact speed you must drive at to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed under all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed for that road. Safe driving may require you to go slower than the posted limit. When conditions are poor, you should slow down.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less distance ahead. Use your headlights properly. Drive slowly enough so you can stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You may cross these lines only for left turns or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, and scooter or skateboard riders when it is safe.

questions.question: How does the DMV's Driver Improvement Program promote traffic safety?

options.text: It suspends your license for 30 days if you are 18 or older with four traffic convictions in 24 months.
It suspends your license for six months if you are under 18 with three traffic convictions.
It restricts your license for 90 days if you are under 18 with two traffic convictions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have multiple traffic convictions or preventable accidents within a certain time period, the Driver Improvement Program may apply penalties. Drivers 18 and older get a 30-day suspension for four convictions in 24 months. Drivers under 18 get a 90-day restriction for two convictions and a six-month suspension for three convictions.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entrance to full parking lots.
Entrance to road construction areas.
Entrance to dead-end streets.
Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road has one-way traffic. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when your turn signals do not work to show other drivers you are changing direction.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
In all of these situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: In all of these situations.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder every time you change your vehicle's position. Do this when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Get ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and wait before moving ahead.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when you think the children are done getting off.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait before moving ahead.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm out, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to check if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to see if anyone is in your blind spot.

questions.question: If you are taking a non-prescription drug, you should:

options.text: Read the labels before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Keep driving no matter what the labels say.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter drugs like cold or allergy medicine can affect your driving. Always check the label for warnings. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you can safely drive while taking the medication.
